Describe the structure of a panel

Source: R/describe_panel.R
describe_panel.Rd

Before deciding which rule a panel must meet, look at what it is: how many units and periods, how many units are observed throughout, who enters and leaves when, where the gaps are, and which participation patterns are common. describe_panel() answers that in one pass and judges nothing; turn what you learn into a rule with ensure_balanced() or ensure_unique().

Usage

describe_panel(data, id, time, periods = NULL, patterns = 10)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database tables in checkpoints.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

time

The period column (one column), e.g. year.

periods

Expected periods. Defaults to those observed in data. Pass them, e.g. 2015:2024, to see a period that is missing for everyone.

patterns

Number of participation patterns to keep, most common first.

Value

An object of class inshape_panel, printed as a summary. It is a list with the counts (n_rows, n_units, n_complete, n_with_gaps, n_gap_cells, n_dup_cells, n_dup_rows, n_missing_id, n_missing_time, n_outside), the periods, and three tibbles: by_period (period, units, entries, exits, gaps), runs (units by number of separate runs of presence) and patterns (pattern, units, share).

Details

It is the panel summary of Stata's xtdescribe, made for population registers: a sudden fall in the number of units in one period, a period with no units at all, or many units with a single missing year are the signs of a broken extract, and they are visible here at a glance.

What is counted

A unit-period is counted once, however many rows it has; the extra rows are reported as duplicates. Rows with a missing period, or a period outside periods, are left out and counted. A missing id is a unit of its own, as in ensure_balanced(), and the rows are counted.

In by_period, entries are the units first observed in a period and exits those last observed in it. Neither is known at the edges, where a unit may have been present before the first or after the last period, so entries is NA in the first period and exits in the last. gaps counts the units absent in a period although they are observed both before and after it.

A participation pattern has one character per period, 1 when the unit is observed and . when not, as in xtdescribe: 11.11 is a unit missing in the middle period of five.

Why it is fast

The id columns are compressed to integer unit ids by one compiled hash pass, without sorting them. The panel then becomes a bit matrix, one bit per unit and period (6 million persons over 64 periods take 48 MB), set in a single pass over the rows; a bit already set is a duplicate. First and last period, counts, runs and patterns are read from the bits with processor bit instructions, so nothing is sorted per row. When the bit matrix would be much larger than the data, as for daily periods over many years, the unit-periods are sorted instead and the patterns, as long as the panel and nearly all different, are left out.

See also

ensure_balanced() to require a balanced panel or no gaps, describe_key() for duplicated keys.

Examples

panel <- data.frame(
  cpr  = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "d", "d", "d"),
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2022, 2022, 2020, 2021, 2022)
)
describe_panel(panel, cpr, year)
#> ── Panel: cpr by year ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 9 rows, 4 units, 3 periods, 2020-2022
#> 
#> • Observed in every period: 2 units (50.0%)
#> • With gaps: 1 unit (25.0%), 1 missing unit-period inside their span
#> • Duplicated unit-periods: 0 (0 extra rows)
#> 
#> By period:
#>     period units entries exits  gaps
#>   1   2020     3      NA     0     0
#>   2   2021     2       0     0     1
#>   3   2022     4       1    NA     0
#> 
#> Most common patterns:
#>     pattern units share
#>   1 111         2 50.0%
#>   2 1.1         1 25.0%
#>   3 ..1         1 25.0%

# The counts are there to use
p <- describe_panel(panel, cpr, year)
p$by_period
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   period units entries exits  gaps
#>    <dbl> <int>   <int> <int> <int>
#> 1   2020     3      NA     0     0
#> 2   2021     2       0     0     1
#> 3   2022     4       1    NA     0
